summary: Practise workplace hazard identification, risk rating and control planning. Explore the five-day HIRA course and its applied curriculum.
lede: Hazard identification and risk assessment training helps safety officers, supervisors and operational team leads turn task observations into documented workplace risk decisions. Participants practise breaking jobs into steps, identifying hazards, rating likelihood and consequence, and selecting controls using the hierarchy of controls and job safety analysis. They also review residual risk, update risk registers and use a simple Bowtie diagram to connect threats, a top event and consequences.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course is designed for people who assess work, assign safety controls or maintain workplace risk records. It suits practitioners who need a repeatable method for turning task observations and incident evidence into documented HIRA decisions.
modules: Job Safety Analysis and Work Steps
prerequisites: Useful preparation: familiarity with routine workplace tasks and basic safety procedures. No specialist HIRA experience or coding is required. Practical exercises use task examples and written assessment templates; advanced Bowtie concepts receive introductory coverage.
